AgentTask.description:
One attempt as the agent running it sees it (08 §Agent-facing).

The identity of the attempt, the run's title and description, the
payload the node was called with, and the work log that is the
inter-stage channel (D4). Everything an agent needs to start, and
nothing an operator route would add.

attempt.description: Which attempt of this node this is, from 1.
attempt.title: Attempt

description.description: The operator's longer brief for the run.
description.title: Description

input.description: The payload the node was enqueued with; null when it had none.
input.title: Input

log.description: The run's work log, oldest first and never truncated, without the `stats` entries.
log.title: Log

output_schema.description: The JSON Schema a submission must fit, when the agent façade running this attempt declared an `output_model`.
output_schema.title: Output Schema

run_id.description: The run the attempt belongs to.
run_id.title: Run Id

task_id.description: This attempt's id; the one the token is for.
task_id.title: Task Id

title.description: The operator's title for the run.
title.title: Title

AgentTask.title: AgentTask

Answer.description:
Answer a request (`POST /api/requests/{id}/answer`, 06 §The model).

``option_id`` for an ``options`` request and ``value`` for a ``text``
or ``form`` one. Both are optional here because ``value`` may
legitimately be any JSON — including ``null``, which is why "which one
was given" cannot be decided by looking at the values alone: the
request's own ``mode`` decides, and the request service refuses the
mismatch with the error code 06 §Errors names for it.

option_id.description: The chosen option, for an `options` request.
option_id.title: Option Id

value.description: The answer, for a `text` or `form` request.
value.title: Value

Answer.title: Answer

AnswerAuthor.description:
Who answered. ``engine`` is a headless fallback: a permission
timeout action or a declined elicitation (06 §Timeouts).
AnswerAuthor.title: AnswerAuthor

AnswerPoll.description:
The result of one long-poll (`GET …/requests/{rid}`, 06 §Surfaces).

``answered`` is the field to branch on. Until it is true the other
two are absent, because a request with no answer has no author
either; once it is true ``answer`` is the chosen ``option_id`` of an
``options`` request and the value of a ``text`` or ``form`` one —
the same folding :class:`~athanore.store.rows.RequestView` does, so
an operator reading the request and the agent reading its answer see
the same value.

Re-delivery is idempotent: nothing is claimed by a poll, so an agent
that lost a response and asked again gets the same answer again.

answer.description: The chosen `option_id`, or the value of a `text` or `form` answer. Null before an answer, and for an answer that was null.
answer.title: Answer

answered.description: Whether an answer has been recorded.
answered.title: Answered

answered_by.description: Who answered: the operator, or the engine on a headless fallback. Null until answered.

AnswerPoll.title: AnswerPoll

Arrivals.description:
How much of an open fan-out has reached a join (04 §Fan-in).

The innermost pending fan-out, which is the one the operator is
waiting on; the SPA renders it as `2 of 3 arrived` (10 §Graph pane).

arrived.description: Branches that have reached the join.
arrived.title: Arrived

Arrivals.title: Arrivals

Ask.description:
A question an agent puts to the operator (`POST …/ask`, 06).

``schema`` is spelled ``schema_`` in Python, as it is in
:class:`~athanore.api.schemas.requests.RequestView`, and keeps
``schema`` as its alias — the name 08 and the curl line of 19 fix on
the wire.

options.description: The choices, for a pick-one question. A bare string is an option that is its own id and label.
options.title: Options

prompt.description: The question, as the operator will read it.
prompt.title: Prompt

schema.description: A JSON Schema the answer must fit, for a form question.
schema.title: Schema

Ask.title: Ask

AskOption.description:
One choice an agent offers the operator (08 §Agent-facing).

``option_id`` is what an answer names and what comes back from the
long-poll; ``name`` is what the operator is shown and defaults to the
id, which is what a bare string in ``options`` is short for.

kind.description: A label for the option; carried through as given.
kind.title: Kind

name.description: What to show the operator; the `option_id` when omitted.
name.title: Name

AskOption.title: AskOption

AskOut.description:
The request an ask opened (08 §Agent-facing).

``mode`` is reported back because the agent did not choose it
directly: it sent options, a schema or neither, and this is what that
was read as — which is also what tells it what shape of answer to
expect from the long-poll.

mode.description: The shape of the answer expected.

request_id.description: The id to poll for an answer.
request_id.title: Request Id

AskOut.title: AskOut

BranchRef.description:
Which branch an output came out of (D58).

The index and the key of each frame, and not the frame's ``fanout`` or
``count``: an output names its branch so a consumer can group by it,
and the task it came from is in the same entry for anything more.

index.title: Index

key.description: The payload that branch was given.
key.title: Key

BranchRef.title: BranchRef

ChunkKind.description:
The kinds of the agent transcript (05 §The ACP client).

``text`` and ``thought`` are the assistant's message and reasoning
chunks, ``tool_call``/``tool_result`` the ACP tool updates, ``notice``
a line the façade itself wrote.
ChunkKind.title: ChunkKind

run_id.description: The id of the run that was queued.
run_id.title: Run Id

EditRun.description:
Change a run's title, its description, or both (`PATCH /api/runs/{id}`).

Both fields are optional and a field that is absent is left alone —
which is why they are optional rather than defaulted: an edit that
sent no description must not blank one. An edit that names neither is
accepted and changes nothing, which is what ``Ops.edit`` does with it:
a patch is not the place to refuse a caller for being redundant.
EditRun.title: EditRun

GraphBranch.description:
The tasks of one node that belong to one branch of a fan-out.

``from_task`` is the fan-out that produced the branch — the
``lineage.from`` of the first task in the branch chain whose parent
returned a list — and is ``null`` for a node reached by a single path,
which has exactly one branch.

tasks.description: This node's attempts in that branch, oldest first.
tasks.title: Tasks

GraphEdge.description:
One arrow of the finalized graph, and how often this run took it.

``from`` is a Python keyword, so the field is ``from_`` and carries
``from`` as its alias — the name 08 fixes on the wire.

GraphEdge.title: GraphEdge

edges.description: Every edge of the finalized graph.
edges.title: Edges

The work log is the inter-stage channel (D4): the engine's failures,

``kind`` is absent on a plain entry.

One node's edges and its options, as 08 §Workflows lists them.

``priority`` and ``retries`` of ``null`` mean "the server default"
and ``timeout`` of ``null`` means no wall-clock cap on one attempt —
the node metadata of 04 §Node options, unresolved, because what the
default *is* belongs to the settings of the server running it.

NodeState.description:
What a node is doing in one run, in 08 §Graph semantics' precedence.

Declared in precedence order, highest first, so the rule is the
member order and not a table kept somewhere else. ``failed`` outranks
``done`` but is itself outranked by ``ready``: a failed attempt whose
retry is queued reports ``ready``, because that retry row exists and
the node is going to run again. ``idle`` means no task of this node
was ever created in this run.

The SPA colours by this alone (10 §Status colours).

An operation that succeeded and has nothing else to report.

``note`` is the one place a router adds a sentence about *how* it
succeeded — 08 §Runs' `{ok, note?}` — and is omitted when there is

Position.description:

Exactly one of the two. ``direction`` swaps with the neighbour above
(``-1``) or below (``+1``) and is a no-op at the ends — still a 200,
reporting the position the run already had. ``index`` is the
**zero-based** list index to move to, clamped to the list; New Run's
"top" is `{"index": 0}` and "bottom" is the default, which needs no
call at all.

get.description:
Everything the agent needs to start, and nothing else (08).

The title and the description are the run's — the brief an operator
submitted — and ``input`` is the payload this node was enqueued with,
``null`` when it had none. ``log`` is the run's work log, oldest
first, uncapped and untruncated: it is the inter-stage channel (D4),
it is bounded by the number of stages rather than by agent output,
and a retried attempt reads the ``failure`` entry that says why the
last one failed.

The ``stats`` entries are dropped (D56). ``output_schema`` is here
only while a façade has declared an ``output_model`` on this
attempt's live context: the ``native`` tooling tier reads it to build
its ``submit_result`` tool (05 §Tooling tiers), and an agent with no
model declared is not required to submit anything.

403 unless the façade running this attempt declared
``ask_policy="http"`` (05 §Policies): an agent cannot grant itself
the right to interrupt a person, and the policy lives on the agent
class the workflow chose. The prompt sections that tell an agent how
to ask are omitted when it is off (19), so a 403 here is an agent
that went looking.

What was sent decides the mode: ``options`` for a pick-one question,
``schema`` for a form — whose answer is validated against that very
schema where it lands, by the validator registered here (06
§Service) — and neither for free text. The request is opened with
``source="agent"`` and no ordinal, because a re-executed attempt does
not reproduce a turn statement for statement (06 §Restart
durability).

The answer does not come back here: the caller polls
``/requests/{rid}``, which is what lets the agent keep its turn
rather than holding this connection open.

get.description:
The answer, waiting up to ``wait`` seconds for one to land.

``wait`` is clamped to :data:`MAX_WAIT` rather than refused, so 19's
instruction — poll with ``?wait=60`` and repeat until it says
``answered`` — is a loop that costs one request per minute and not a
spin. The wait ends the moment the answer is recorded, not when the
clamp expires.

A request of **another** task is a 404, not someone else's answer: a
token names one attempt and this route reads only what that attempt
opened (12 §Task tokens).

Nothing is claimed. An agent that lost a response and asked again
gets the same answer again, which is what makes a dropped connection
cost nothing (06 §Service).

post.description:
Record a value for this attempt, if it fits what was asked for.

With an ``output_model`` declared, a misfit is a 422 carrying
``errors`` and ``schema`` and nothing is stored: the agent reads the
two in its own tool output and can fix the shape inside the same turn
(05 §Submissions). The rejection is also left on the context as
``ctx.last_rejection``, which is what 19's repair turn quotes back if
the turn ends without a valid submission.

With none declared, any JSON is stored as it arrived.

Submitting twice is not an error: the **latest valid** payload wins
(D5), and a body reads it with ``submissions.latest()``. A submission
never routes anything — the node body decides — so an agent cannot
move its own task.

Pausing every run and then waiting for `tasks_in_progress` to reach
zero here is how an operator drains a server before stopping it.

Whether this server wants a token, and whether this request has one.

Never requires one itself: a request with no credential on a server
that wants one gets a 200 saying `{"auth": "token", "authenticated":
false}`, which is the client's cue to ask for a token.

get.description:
The requests of every run, or of one, oldest first.

"Pending" is narrower than "unanswered": a request whose task has
ended is **stale** and leaves the inbox, because an answer to it
would reach nobody (06 §Restart durability). It stays in the run's
own history, and ``pending=false`` here shows it too, with
``stale: true`` on it.

An application with no store holds no requests and answers with an
empty list; a ``run`` that names no run is a filter that matches
nothing rather than a 404.

``option_id`` for an ``options`` request and ``value`` for a ``text``
or ``form`` one; the request's own ``mode`` decides which of the two
is read, so a ``value`` sent to an ``options`` request is not an
answer that request could have (06 §Service).

The response is the **updated** view rather than the answer row (08
§Requests): the SPA re-renders the card it just answered, and
``pending``, ``answer`` and ``answered_by`` are all part of what
changed. The author is ``user`` — this route is the operator's, and
the other author, ``engine``, belongs to the headless fallbacks that
record an answer without a person (06 §Timeouts).
